scenes.tts: Push a small current into a resting cell. Does the voltage jump to its new level?
scenes.visual: A cell with a pipette. A current trace (top) and an empty voltage trace (bottom) on shared time axes. The question appears.
scenes.narration: Push a small current into a resting cell. Does the voltage jump to its new level?

scenes.tts: In current clamp, you set the current flowing into the cell, and you record its voltage.
scenes.visual: Labels: current clamp; you set I (top trace), you record Vm (bottom trace).
scenes.narration: In current clamp, you set the current flowing into the cell, and you record its voltage.

scenes.tts: Give our cell a small negative step of current. It pushes the voltage down, away from threshold.
scenes.visual: The current trace steps down to −100 pA from 0 to 60 ms. The voltage axis is marked −71.2 mV at rest.
scenes.narration: Give our cell a small negative step of current. It pushes the voltage down, away from threshold.

scenes.tts: So does the voltage jump, the instant the current switches on?
scenes.visual: On screen: Pause. Does Vm jump when the current step begins?
scenes.narration: So does the voltage jump, the instant the current switches on?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: No. It starts moving at once, but smoothly. Steeply at first, then bending over toward a plateau.
scenes.visual: The voltage trace draws live: flat, then a curve that falls steeply and bends over toward a plateau.
scenes.narration: No. It starts moving at once, but smoothly. Steeply at first, then bending over toward a plateau.

scenes.tts: When the step ends, it relaxes back to rest along the same kind of curve.
scenes.visual: At 60 ms the current returns to zero; the voltage curve relaxes back toward −71.2 mV.
scenes.narration: When the step ends, it relaxes back to rest along the same kind of curve.

scenes.tts: The reason is that the membrane stores charge. The thin bilayer between two salty solutions is a capacitor.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the membrane: a thin bilayer with opposite charges lined up on its two faces. Label: capacitor (C).
scenes.narration: The reason is that the membrane stores charge. The thin bilayer between two salty solutions is a capacitor.

scenes.tts: The leak channels are resistors, side by side with it.
scenes.visual: A circuit diagram builds: a capacitor and a resistor in parallel. Label: leak = resistor.
scenes.narration: The leak channels are resistors, side by side with it.

scenes.tts: Picture a straight-sided tank with a drain. The water level is the size of the voltage change. The tank's width is the capacitance.
scenes.visual: A straight-sided water tank appears beside the trace. Labels: level = size of ΔV (whichever way Vm moves), width = C.
scenes.narration: Picture a straight-sided tank with a drain. The water level is the size of the voltage change. The tank's width is the capacitance.

scenes.tts: The drain is the leak, and its outflow grows with the level. The injected current is a hose pouring in.
scenes.visual: A drain at the bottom labelled leak (g_total), outflow proportional to level; a hose above labelled injected current, size of I.
scenes.narration: The drain is the leak, and its outflow grows with the level. The injected current is a hose pouring in.

scenes.tts: At first the level has not risen, so nothing extra drains away. All the inflow raises the level.
scenes.visual: Hose on; the drain shows no flow yet; the level starts to rise while the voltage trace starts to fall: both show the change growing. The steep start of the trace is highlighted.
scenes.narration: At first the level has not risen, so nothing extra drains away. All the inflow raises the level.

scenes.tts: That sets the starting slope: current divided by capacitance.
scenes.visual: On screen: initial slope = I / C. On screen only: −100 pA / 200 pF = −0.5 mV per ms.
scenes.narration: That sets the starting slope: current divided by capacitance.

scenes.tts: As the level rises, more water drains out, so the level rises more slowly.
scenes.visual: The drain flow grows as the level rises; the trace bends over in step.
scenes.narration: As the level rises, more water drains out, so the level rises more slowly.

scenes.tts: It stops rising when the drain carries all the inflow. That is the plateau.
scenes.visual: Drain flow equals hose flow; the level holds; the trace flattens. Label: plateau.
scenes.narration: It stops rising when the drain carries all the inflow. That is the plateau.

scenes.tts: Now back to the ropes. The injected current is a steady extra pull on the marker.
scenes.visual: The voltage scale from earlier chapters returns. A teal arrow pushes the marker left, labelled injected current, the same size wherever the marker sits.
scenes.narration: Now back to the ropes. The injected current is a steady extra pull on the marker.

scenes.tts: The ropes stretch until together they cancel it. So the balance point shifts by the current divided by the total leak.
scenes.caption: The ropes stretch until together they cancel it. So the balance point shifts by the current divided by the total leak, I / g_total.
scenes.visual: The ghost balance point jumps left at once by I / g_total; the real marker follows along the curve. On screen only: −100 pA / 10 nS = −10 mV; −71.2 → −81.2 mV.
scenes.narration: The ropes stretch until together they cancel it. So the balance point shifts by the current divided by the total leak, I / g_total.

scenes.tts: That shift for each unit of current is the input resistance. It is one over the total leak.
scenes.visual: On screen: Rin = ΔV / I = 1 / g_total.
scenes.narration: That shift for each unit of current is the input resistance. It is one over the total leak.

scenes.tts: For our cell, that is one hundred megohms.
scenes.caption: For our cell, that is 100 MΩ.
scenes.visual: The 10 nS tag from chapter 2 slides in, relabelled: ohmic model, 10 nS fixed leak. On screen only: 1 / 10 nS = 100 MΩ.
scenes.narration: For our cell, that is 100 MΩ.

scenes.tts: The balance point moves at once. The voltage follows it, at a pace set by capacitance and leak.
scenes.visual: The ghost marker sits at the new level; the real marker slides after it.
scenes.narration: The balance point moves at once. The voltage follows it, at a pace set by capacitance and leak.

scenes.tts: That pace is the time constant. It equals capacitance divided by total leak.
scenes.visual: On screen: τ = Rin × C = C / g_total.
scenes.narration: That pace is the time constant. It equals capacitance divided by total leak.

scenes.tts: In one time constant, the voltage gets about sixty-three percent of the way. Not all of it.
scenes.caption: In one time constant, the voltage gets about 63% of the way. Not all of it.
scenes.visual: On the trace, a flag at one τ marks 63% of the final change; faint marks at 2τ (86%) and 3τ (95%).
scenes.narration: In one time constant, the voltage gets about 63% of the way. Not all of it.

scenes.tts: For our cell, the time constant is twenty milliseconds.
scenes.caption: For our cell, the time constant is 20 ms.
scenes.visual: On screen only: 200 pF / 10 nS = 20 ms. The 63% flag sits at 20 ms, at Vm ≈ −77.52 mV on the absolute-voltage trace, with a bracket from rest labelled ΔV = −6.32 mV, 63% of the final −10 mV change.
scenes.narration: For our cell, the time constant is 20 ms.

scenes.tts: More leak means a smaller change, reached sooner.
scenes.visual: A second tank with a bigger drain: the level stops lower and sooner. A second trace overlays: smaller and faster.
scenes.narration: More leak means a smaller change, reached sooner.

scenes.tts: A change also lingers after its input ends. So inputs close together in time overlap and add.
scenes.visual: Two brief inputs a little apart in time: the second rides on the tail of the first, and the summed peak is higher than either alone.
scenes.narration: A change also lingers after its input ends. So inputs close together in time overlap and add.

scenes.tts: That is temporal summation. A longer time constant widens the window for overlap.
scenes.visual: The same two inputs with a longer τ, both drawn with the same isolated peak: more of the first is left when the second arrives. Label: temporal summation.
scenes.narration: That is temporal summation. A longer time constant widens the window for overlap.

scenes.tts: The total leak sets how big a nudge is, and how fast the voltage gets there.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: total leak sets how big (Rin = 1/g_total) and how fast (τ = C/g_total).
scenes.narration: The total leak sets how big a nudge is, and how fast the voltage gets there.
